title: Little River Casino golf outing raises more than $68,000 for Manistee nonprofits - NewsBreak
text:
By News Advocate Staff ,
12 hours ago Little River Casino Resort hosted its 27th Annual Charity Golf Classic July 10, 2026. Proceeds from the event will be distributed to numerous nonprofit organizations. Representatives of those some of those organizations are pictured from left to right: Michael Schrader, Donald Vadeboncoeur, Linda Gamache-Chick, George Goodrich, Chad Eckhardt, Nancy Supran, Gene Lagerquist, Doug LaFleur, Steve Growcock, Sawyer Hendrickson, Logan Tomaszewski, Linda Albee, Jodie Phillips and Linda Wright. (Courtesy of Little River Casino Resort) Little River Casino Resort hosted its 27th Annual Charity Golf Classic on July 10 at Manistee National Golf and Resort.
This year’s golf scramble drew 154 golfers and raised more than $68,000 to benefit charities serving Manistee and the surrounding area, according to Chad Eckhardt Little River Casino Resort player development manager.
“Little River established the Charity Golf Outing back in 1999, the year the casino first opened for business,” Eckhardt said. “And I’m happy to say it continues to be a great success for everyone involved. It really is a good feeling to be able to give back to our local communities.”
With volunteer support and contributions from the casino resort’s many vendors, the annual event has raised a total of $1,315,993 in private and business donations over the last 27 years, said Eckhardt.
Proceeds from the 2026 Charity Golf Outing will be distributed to numerous nonprofit organizations, including the following:
A Kid Again Manistee Discovery Cove Circle Rocking S Children’s Farm Communities Overcoming Violent Encounters Manistee Amphitheater Foundation Alternatives for Area Youth/The Rec at Sands Park Miss Sawyers Kids with a Cause Spirit of the Woods Conservation Club VFW Walsh Post No. 4499 VFW Bear Creek Post No. 6333 Little River Casino Resort underwrites all costs associated with the event and donates 100% of all the monies from participant fees and sponsorship funds raised.
